title: A Deadline for the Debt
premise: Rafael Halloran spent six years laundering himself out of the covert financial unit that trained him, building a quiet life auditing clean money and lying to the woman he loves about who he used to be. When a calendar invitation arrives from his handler—dead for three months—he's pulled back into a network that faked her death to test whether its assets can still be activated. To survive, Rafael must dismantle the organization that made him, but every account he burns exposes another lie he told Elena, forcing him to choose between protecting her and trusting her with the truth. In the end, he trades his own anonymity for hers, handing the evidence to prosecutors and walking into custody, while Elena—having read everything—waits outside the courthouse anyway.
about_author: E. M. Oyelaran is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction full-time. They write thrillers about people whose ledgers never balance against their consciences, and live in Lagos and Lisbon depending on the season.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Six years into his quiet life as a compliance auditor, Rafael receives a meeting request from Marguerite Voss, his dead handler, scheduled for tomorrow at 9 a.m. He checks the go-bag under the floorboards, then lies to Elena about a work trip. The beat is dread disguised as routine—the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Rafael, flashback-woven. At the meeting site—an empty marina office—he finds only a burner phone preloaded with one file: proof someone inside the old network is still moving his frozen accounts. Interleaved flashbacks show Voss training him to disappear. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing invisibility was an illusion he was sold.

chapters.title: What Elena Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Home alone, Elena finds a receipt from a city Rafael claimed never to have visited. Her suspicion is tender, not paranoid—she's known he has locked rooms in himself and chose patience. She calls his sister for corroboration and gets a hesitation that confirms more than any answer. Beat: love strained by half-truths.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Following the money trail, Rafael identifies a live account only three people could have opened: himself, Voss, and the trainer called Anselm. A near-miss with a surveillance team in Rotterdam proves the network is hunting him too. Beat: hunter becoming hunted, adrenaline sharpening into resolve—he decides to burn it all down.

chapters.title: Anselm
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael confronts Anselm at a Geneva private bank, expecting a traitor and finding a frightened man: Anselm reveals Voss faked her death to smoke out which assets could still be leveraged—and that Rafael was the target asset all along. Beat: betrayal reframed; the mentor's death was a recruitment letter.

chapters.title: Collateral
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Elena is approached by a charming 'colleague' of Rafael's who knows too much about her. She records the conversation on instinct, realizing she's being used as leverage. Beat: fear transmuting into agency—she stops waiting for Rafael's truth and starts investigating on her own terms.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Alive
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Voss contacts him directly, offering absolution and a partnership: help her seize the network's ledger and they both walk free. Rafael sees the trap—she needs a fall guy—but plays along long enough to copy the master ledger. Beat: the student outmaneuvering the teacher, grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Everything He Buried
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rafael/Elena. Rafael comes home to confess; Elena meets him at the door with her recording already playing. The truth detonates between them—not just the crimes, but the years of curated lies. Beat: the novel's emotional climax; love against duty becomes love versus deception, and she walks out.

chapters.title: Burn Rate
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. With hours before Voss can trigger the network's contingency, Rafael executes his plan: simultaneous disclosures to prosecutors in four jurisdictions, each timed to freeze the network's accounts and corner Voss. A final confrontation at the data center ends with Voss arrested and Rafael surrendering voluntarily. Beat: duty fulfilled at maximum personal cost.

chapters.title: After the Audit
chapters.summary: POV Elena, closing on Rafael. Months later, Rafael awaits sentencing, having traded testimony for a reduced term. Elena visits with the ledger of their life—letters, questions, no guarantees—but she came. Beat: resolution without absolution; inheritance of a shared future built on finally-true ground, and the possibility that love survives audit.
